mutation.diagnosis: The intermediate combines a cross-sectional price reversal/strength signal with a negated volume-price correlation via equal-weight additive ranking. A single window mutation on the correlation lookback is the most auditable improvement: the 60-day co-movement window may be too slow for a weekly-rebalanced factor, so shortening it sharpens the volume-price interaction and likely stabilizes rank IC without touching the combined mechanism.

expected_metric_effects.composite_score: expected to rise modestly due to sharper volume interaction while preserving complementary price signal
expected_metric_effects.mean_rank_ic_10d: expected to improve as faster volume-price correlation better aligns with weekly rebalance horizon
expected_metric_effects.monthly_stability: expected to remain stable or improve slightly from more responsive volume-price signal

mutation.diagnosis: The intermediate blends a 60-day price-volume correlation (negated) with a 10-day close ts_rank (negated). Both sub-signals are raw cross-sectional quantities with different scales: the correlation ranges roughly [-1,1] while the negated 10-day ts_rank ranges [-1,0]. Their raw add can let scale and cross-sectional distribution differences dominate rather than the intended complementary information. A single window change on the ts_rank component is the smallest auditable mutation that can reduce short-term noise in the rank component while preserving the full combined parent mechanism, orientations, and every operator.

expected_metric_effects.rank_ic_percentile: Modest change; lengthening the rank window from 10 to 15 may slightly reduce short-term noise and stabilize the complementary short-horizon component.
expected_metric_effects.rank_icir_20d: Potential marginal improvement from a less noisy ts_rank component feeding the blended factor, while preserving the negative orientation and complementary structure.

Its raw cross-sectional scale varies over time, which can make weekly top-k selection unstable; applying a cross-sectional rank normalization standardizes the combined signal without altering its economic mechanism.

factor_spec.description: This factor negatively orients and then cross-sectionally ranks the two parent signals before summing. Parent A is a 10-day time-series rank of close; Parent B is a 30-day correlation between close-to-close returns and log volume change (reduced from 40 days). Both raw parents have training_direction=-1, so they are negated to align with positive expected IC. Cross-sectional ranking equalizes scales and keeps the composite robust. The only change from the intermediate is the correlation window, from 40 to 30.

The composite is well diversified but relies on fixed, somewhat arbitrary windows. A single window mutation on the 40-day correlation window tests whether tightening the return-volume co-movement horizon to 30 days sharpens the signal's responsiveness while preserving the exact combined parent mechanism and all operators, fields, min_periods, and other window values.

mutation.diagnosis: The intermediate blends a longer-horizon temporal extreme signal (negated 30-day index of high minus low) with a short-horizon support-proximity signal (5-day rolling min low over close), both z-scored and summed. The weak point is the short-horizon leg's window sensitivity: a 5-day rolling min is noisy and may flip quickly, adding variance that undermines the stability and ICIR gains the blend is meant to deliver. A single window change to the rolling-min leg, widening it from 5 to 10 days, smooths that support measure while preserving the exact blended mechanism and all other parameters.

expected_metric_effects.mean_rank_ic_10d: Expected to remain comparable or improve due to reduced short-leg noise.
expected_metric_effects.mean_rank_ic_20d: Expected to improve as the smoothed support leg lowers signal variance in the blended factor.
expected_metric_effects.mean_rank_ic_5d: May dip slightly versus the 5-day parent leg because the support signal decays more slowly, but should remain positive.
expected_metric_effects.monthly_stability: Expected to improve modestly from reduced turnover in the short-horizon support component.
expected_metric_effects.rank_icir_20d: Expected to improve because a less noisy short-horizon leg reduces variance in the combined signal.

factor_spec.description: Window mutation of the G02-CROSS-008 intermediate: the negated trailing ts_rank of close is lengthened from 60 to 120 days and added to the unchanged low/close ratio. Slower positioning leg reduces turnover and noise while retaining the intraday recovery component.
factor_spec.name: Negated Rank120 Close Position plus Low/Close

mutation.diagnosis: The intermediate combines a negated 60-day close ts_rank with the low/close ratio, and both components operate at very different scales. The raw ts_rank is bounded in [0,1] before negation, while low/close sits between 0 and 1 but with a small dynamic range and daily noise. Simply adding them lets the noisier low/close term dominate short-term swings and obscures the slower positioning signal. Cross-sectional normalization of each leg would align the scales, but a single-window operator change keeps the combined mechanism intact. Widening the close rank window from 60 to 120 reduces turnover in the positioning leg and smooths the composite while preserving the negate/add structure and the low/close term exactly.

expected_metric_effects.monthly_stability: improve

mutation.mutation_description: Change only the ts_rank window on the close field from 60 to 120, leaving the negate, add, divide(low,close), all min_periods, and every other node property unchanged.
